title: The Fellowship's Dependency
philosophicalAnchor: When the Rohan app requires horses==1.0 and Gondor needs horses==2.0, isolation becomes essential. Virtual environments create sacred spaces where each application can honor its own dependencies without conflict.
pythonConcept: virtual environments, venv, sys.prefix, sys.base_prefix, requirements.txt, dependency management
briefDescription: Containerize conflicting applications in their own virtual environments to resolve dependency conflicts between the Rohan and Gondor apps.
theoryPillar: Virtual environments provide isolated Python installations with their own site-packages. This prevents global package conflicts where different projects require different versions of the same dependency.
anchorPillar: The Rohan app requires horses==1.0 but Gondor needs horses==2.0. Installing both globally causes one to overwrite the other, crashing the first app. Each needs its own sacred space.
triggerPillar: The Fellowship's applications are crashing! Dependency conflicts arise when multiple projects need different versions of the same package. Global installation cannot resolve this.
realityPillar: sys.prefix vs sys.base_prefix detects virtual environment. python -m venv creates environments. source .venv/bin/activate (Linux/Mac) or .venv\Scripts\activate (Windows) enters the environment. requirements.txt specifies exact (==) and minimum (>=) versions.
